title: Describing Nouns: adj + 的, clause + 的, 第
description: When an adjective needs 的 (好朋友 vs 很好的朋友), relative clauses with 的 (the person who …), and ordinals with 第.

points.title: Adjective + (的) + noun
points.summary: One-syllable adjectives often attach directly: 好朋友, 新书. With 很 or a two-syllable adjective, use 的: 很好**的**朋友, 聪明**的**孩子.
points.body:
- 一本**新**书.
- 一个很聪明**的**孩子.
- ~~很好朋友~~ ✗
examples: I have a very good friend.

points.title: Clause + 的 + noun: the … who / that
points.summary: In Chinese the description (a whole clause) comes **before** the noun, joined by 的.
points.body:
- 在那儿工作**的**人 (the people who work there).
- 跟你说话**的**那个人 (that person who was talking to you).
examples: The people who work there are all young.

points.title: 第 + number: ordinals
points.summary: 第 (dì) + number (+ measure word) = first, second …. 第二天 = the next day.
points.body:
- 这是我**第**一次来中国.
- **第**二天 (the next day).
examples: This is my first time in China.

notes: 得 follows a verb.
地 comes before a verb.
第 goes before a number (第一).
The description comes before the noun.
很 goes before the adjective.
With 很, the adjective needs 的.
questions.translation: I have a very good friend.

notes: 很 must come before the adjective.
With 很 you'd need 的: 很新的书.
The adjective comes before the noun.
得 needs a description after it.
第 goes before a number (第一).
地 comes before a verb.
questions.translation: The people who work there are all young.

questions.prompt: Which phrase means 'the person who is reading a book'?
notes: 在 goes before 看.
的 joins the clause to the noun.
The noun comes last.
questions.translation: the person who is reading a book

notes: 得 needs a description after it.
地 comes before a verb.
第 goes before a number (第一).
questions.translation: I don't know the person who was talking to you.

notes: 我的一次 isn't the ordinal — 第 makes 'first'.
每一次 = 'every time' — 这是我每一次… isn't grammatical.
这一次 = 'this time' — 这是我这一次 isn't grammatical.
questions.translation: This is my first time in China.

questions.prompt: In 「{我|wǒ}{第二|dì-èr}{天|tiān}{就|jiù}{回|huí}{去|qù}{了|le}。」, what does 第二天 mean?
notes: The day after tomorrow = 后天.
Two days = 两天.
Every other day = 每隔一天.
questions.translation: I went back the next day.
